correctness.rationale: Ordinary insertion/deletion/substitution distance was recomputed independently by a length-5 Levenshtein dynamic program for all 32 words. The 211-edge compatibility graph has exactly 28 four-vertex cliques and no five-vertex cliques (all C(32,5) tested), so optimum is four. For every extremizer, subtracting a codeword yields a four-element XOR-closed subspace: all 28 are affine binary 2-flats. There are 14 directions and 2 eligible cosets per direction exchanged by complement; the six mutual edit distances split as 18 with five 3s and one 4, and 10 with four 3s and two 4s. A separate networkx GraphMatcher isomorphism enumeration of the EXACT 32-vertex graph finds precisely four automorphisms, which agree with reversal and global bit complement, inducing eight maximum-code orbits of sizes 2,2,4,4,4,4,4,4. This is a provably exhaustive finite proof, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: Only ordinary Levenshtein edit distance and this fixed length/threshold; ambient edit-space graph automorphisms and finite compatibility graph automorphisms need not coincide a priori.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Known global edit-space automorphism group contains complement and reversal, but this general theorem neither classifies finite optimal codes nor implies the finite compatibility-graph automorphism group order; exact clique counts require additional finite computation.
